arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was identified originating from a malicious IP (203.0.113.88). Initial access was achieved via a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell script from Outlook, leading to the execution of a malicious DLL via rundll32. The attacker established C2 communication over port 443. Containment actions included revocation of four critical service accounts and forced credential rotation across 200 production hosts via Ansible.

timeline.description: Initial scan from external IP 203.0.113.88 detected by IDS against host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101).
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook, which spawned an encoded PowerShell process.
PowerShell executed malicious command, launching rundll32 with a DLL from the Temp directory.
rundll32 established outbound C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443.
Incident response initiated. Four critical service accounts (svc-backup, svc-sql-prod, admin-deploy, svc-monitoring) had credentials revoked via IAM/PAM system.
Ansible playbook 'emergency_credential_rotate.yml' executed across 200 production hosts, forcing local password expiry and SSH key revocation.

rule Malicious_Dll_Loading_via_Rundll32 {
    meta:
        description = "Detects unsigned DLL executed via rundll32 from Temp directory"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        date = "2026-05-05"
    strings:
        $rundll32 = "rundll32.exe" nocase
        $temp_path = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" nocase
        $start_func = ",Start" nocase
    condition:
        $rundll32 and $temp_path and $start_func
}

rule Malicious_Dll_Loading_via_Rundll32 {

        description = "Detects unsigned DLL executed via rundll32 from Temp directory"
